purpose: select the highest measured power-of-two internal coupled integration factor that preserves 64 outer ticks per second and meets independent numerical and full-workload timing gates

comparison.control_interpretation: commands and burn boundaries remain indexed by the 64 Hz outer ticks; internal substeps do not consume extra commands

oracle.qualification: existing independent universal-variable conic, analytic rocket, and refined mutual point-mass RK4 reference; no core imports
oracle.gmatscope: previous matched-model GMAT results remain corroborating evidence; no repeat needed unless a new mismatch arises

refinement_floor_exemption.condition: both position errors and both velocity errors, at selected and half-selected internal factors, must all be below their respective floors

additional_physics_gates.earth_and_moon_max_position_and_velocity: each strictly less than legacy factor 1 error
additional_physics_gates.finite_burn_mass: mass at every exported time must be decimal-exact equal across selected, coarser and legacy outputs; each also retains the analytic mass gate
additional_physics_gates.coverage: every one-second sample from zero through the declared endpoint, with tick equal to seconds times 64

held_out.velocity_rounding: each Cartesian component rounded once to nearest nm/s; oracle uses those actual rounded values
held_out.selection_boundary: choose factor using nominal cases and timing first, then evaluate this case at selected, half-selected and legacy factors; do not tune to the held-out result
held_out.gates: same orbital absolute/conservation/refinement gates, plus strict position and velocity improvement over legacy

timing.display_scope: headless FlightView serialization and canonical state SHA, with the full 11-body catalogue; network and GPU/rendering time excluded
timing.identity: each workload has a consistent identifier and definition hash across factors and platforms; coast and alternating coupled burn/rotation/assist runs are measured separately
timing.selection: screen factors first, then fully measure the selected and next-higher factor on both platforms and both workloads; selected must pass and next-higher must fail at least one timing gate, unless selected is the maximum factor 32
timing.unmeasured: short screening runs cannot establish acceptance. a confirmed selected/next-higher bracket supports the configured choice; the stronger globally highest-measured claim requires complete measurements of every higher factor

boundaries: no changes to the numerical thresholds after seeing candidate results
no claim about error extrema between the exported one-second samples
same-model numerical accuracy is separate from Horizons model discrepancy and cross-device byte identity
fixed substep count only; no timing-driven or floating adaptive integration decisions
runtime headroom is measured on the specified hardware and workload, not a guarantee for every desktop or visible renderer
